overlays.name: Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District
overlays.effect: No new Liquor Stores. A Restaurant operating as a Bona Fide Eating Place may serve alcohol (licenses may be transferred in from inside or outside the SUD), as may non-profit theaters, bowling alleys/mini-golf with an integrated Restaurant, single-screen movie theaters (beer and wine) and ABC Type 90 music venues. East of the western boundary of the Mission Street NCT and north of Cesar Chavez Street, any new Restaurant requires CU and new ABC Type 75 (brewpub) licenses are prohibited. Good-neighbor operating conditions (§ 202.2 plus lighting and window-signage limits) apply.

filing_playbook.action: Verify that a Type 42 or Type 48 license is available for transfer from a bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD; if not, the concept cannot proceed as a bar use.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Contact SF Planning (Mission Alcohol SUD administrator) to confirm whether any in-district bar licenses are available for transfer. If none exist, the concept must be re-framed as a restaurant (Type 41 eating place) with entertainment accessory to meals, not a standalone bar. Include this confirmation in the pre-application meeting notes.

filing_playbook.action: File for a pre-application meeting with SF Planning to discuss the bar CUA, Mission Alcohol SUD license-transfer requirement, and likely conditions.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Request a pre-application meeting under Planning Code §312. Explain that the concept is a 40-seat beer-and-wine bar with limited kitchen and live music until midnight, and that you are seeking to transfer a Type 42 license from another bar within the Mission Alcohol SUD per §249.60. Ask what conditions (hours, sound, security, good-neighbor policy) the Commission will require and whether the current restaurant use simplifies the hearing.

filing_playbook.action: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning for bar use, along with the required neighborhood notification and environmental review.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Frame the project as a conversion of an existing restaurant to a beer-and-wine bar with occasional live music, emphasizing the transfer of an in-district bar license per §249.60 and the limited scale (40 seats, beer and wine only, no dancing). Commit to a good-neighbor policy, sound monitoring, posted complaint hotline, and hours of operation ending at 1 a.m. or earlier if the Commission requests. Attach an acoustic study showing the space can meet residential sound limits, a security plan, and letters of support from the neighborhood association and nearby businesses.

filing_playbook.action: In parallel with the CUA, file for a Place of Entertainment permit intake meeting with the Entertainment Commission.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Email the Deputy Director to confirm zoning eligibility and request an intake meeting. Explain that live music will be occasional (1–2 nights per week), end by midnight, and occupy no more than ⅓ of the floor area. Commit to the Good Neighbor Policy, sound-level monitoring, and an annual report on complaints. Attach the same acoustic study and security plan submitted with the CUA, and state that the POE application will be complete once the CUA is approved.

filing_playbook.action: Once the CUA is approved, file the Place of Entertainment permit application with the Entertainment Commission, including the $2,708 fee, posted notice, and Police/Planning referrals.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the POE application online with proof of the approved CUA, the lease, the acoustic study, the security plan, and the good-neighbor policy. Post the yellow notice at the premises for 30 days and notify neighbors within 300 ft. Coordinate with SFPD and Planning for their referral sign-offs before the Commission hearing.

filing_playbook.action: After CUA approval, apply to ABC for the Type 42 license, including the city's Public Convenience or Necessity finding if required by the undue-concentration review.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the ABC Type 42 application with proof of the approved CUA, the lease, the seller's permit, the entity registration, and workers' comp insurance. Include the Planning Commission's PCN finding letter if ABC requests it due to high license density. Post the 30-day public notice at the premises and comply with ABC's transfer and investigation timeline.

filing_playbook.action: File the building permit application with DBI for tenant improvements, including DPH plan check, Fire, and Planning routing.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit stamped architectural plans showing the limited kitchen, bar layout, ADA upgrades, restrooms, and any soundproofing or HVAC work. Route the application to DPH for health plan check, Fire for hood and suppression review, and Planning for zoning sign-off. Indicate that the CUA and POE permit are approved and attach copies. Schedule the DPH pre-final inspection at 80% completion and the final inspection before opening.

filing_playbook.action: After the final DBI and DPH inspections, apply for the Health Permit to Operate and obtain ASCAP, BMI, and RBS certifications for staff in the final two weeks before opening.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the Health Permit application online with the Business Account Number, the certified food manager certificate, and proof that the building permit final was issued. Schedule the DPH final inspection. Enroll staff in ABC RBS training and obtain ASCAP and BMI public performance licenses before the first day of music programming.

timeline_cost.path: CUA for bar use + Mission Alcohol SUD license transfer + Place of Entertainment permit + ABC Type 42 with PCN finding + building permit and health permit.
timeline_cost.notes: The critical path is the Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days per catalog) plus the Place of Entertainment permit (45–120 days, filed after CUA approval). ABC Type 42 processing (60–150 days) runs in parallel with the POE permit once the CUA is approved, but undue-concentration review will add 1–3 months and require a Public Convenience or Necessity finding from Planning. Building permit plan review (14–120 days) can start after the CUA is approved. Total timeline: 8–16 months from CUA filing to opening. Government fees include CUA application ~$3,100, POE permit $2,708, ABC Type 42 $1,000–$1,600, Health plan check $828–$2,207, Health Permit $470, Building permit $800–$15,000 (depending on construction cost), plus state/federal registrations ~$300. The largest uncertainty is whether a Type 42 or 48 license is available for transfer from within the Mission Alcohol SUD; if none exists, the concept cannot be approved as a bar and must be re-framed as a restaurant with accessory entertainment. The second risk is the CUA hearing: the only bar CUA filed on this block was withdrawn, and the records show no new bar approvals in the modern SUD era. Plan for 10–12 months and $12,000–$18,000 in fees if a transferable license is secured and the CUA is approved; 16+ months if the undue-concentration PCN process or a CUA appeal adds delay.
timeline_cost.verification_note: Day and fee ranges follow from cited catalogs, but records do not state the uncertainties, risks, or whether a license is available for transfer.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St sits in the NCT-VALENCIA zoning district where bars require Conditional Use Authorization, and the site falls within the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District which mandates that any new bar use must transfer a license from another bar within the SUD—not from outside or from a restaurant. The parcel currently holds an active Type 41 eating-place license (Sarita's Grill & Beer, issued 2023) and has operated as a restaurant continuously since at least 1999. The immediate block is saturated: 9 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft and 24 food/drink businesses within 500 ft, triggering undue-concentration risk. Only 3 comparable dated use decisions appear within 1,000 ft over the past 10 years (1 approved, 2 withdrawn)—too few to establish an approval rate—but the records show no bar CUAs approved on Valencia between 20th and 21st Streets in the modern SUD era.
data_gaps: No hearing transcripts or decision text available for the 2011 CUA at 991-999 Valencia (Type 41→47 upgrade) to understand what conditions or findings the Commission required.
ABC license conditions for the active licenses within 500 ft are not exposed in the dataset; cannot assess whether neighboring premises operate under restrictive conditions.
The records do not reveal whether any Type 42 or 48 licenses currently exist within the Mission Alcohol SUD boundaries that might be available for transfer.
No base rate data for bar CUAs specifically within the Mission Alcohol SUD; the 3 counted decisions include a restaurant license upgrade and withdrawn applications, not new bar authorizations.
Entertainment Commission hearing records for the nearby POE permits (998 Valencia, 2500 Mission) are not included; cannot determine what soundproofing, hours, or capacity conditions were imposed.
